messages:
From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@acmedata.com>

Cc: procurement@acmedata.com
Date: 2026-02-08T09:14:00Z
Subject: Pricing exhibit questions — slope protection + invoice mapping

Soojin,

Thanks for the draft order schedule. Two quick items from our procurement review:

1) The "slope protection" language in Exhibit B says Redwood will smooth price changes over a 90-day window, but the drafting doesn't define the trigger point or the calculation method (percent of delta vs absolute token volume). Can you confirm how the adjustment denominator is supposed to be calculated?

2) Our AP team needs a clear invoice-metric mapping so we can automate charge recognition. The current exhibit references "monthly usage metric" but our system requires a unique invoice line item code and mapping table. Can you provide the mapping or let us know if Redwood will provide an invoice appendix?

We attached our internal procurement checklist (Procurement_Checklist_2026.pdf) — not redlines. Happy to hop on a quick call if it's easier.

Best,
Jordan Mills
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Data

Subject: RE: Pricing exhibit questions — slope protection + invoice mapping

Jordan — thanks for the clear notes. I pulled the order schedule into a focused redline and added two options for the slope calculation: an absolute-token approach and a relative %-delta approach. See attached (soojin_redline_v1.docx).

High-level answers:
- Trigger: adjustments kick when monthly billable token usage changes by >15% versus rolling 90-day average (option A), or when month-over-month delta exceeds 10% of prior month (option B). We flagged both in the doc for legal to weigh in.
- Denominator: option A uses the rolling 90-day token average; option B uses prior-month token total. Both produce different smoothing math — I called out the expected effect on Monthly Service Fees.
- Invoice mapping: we can provide a two-line mapping appendix (Invoice Code, Metric, Unit of Measure). I've asked LAURA to confirm the canonical invoice code convention we use for reserved vs metered lines.

Next steps: Karthik — can you propose final clause language for the two options? Laura — can you confirm the invoice code pattern and whether we can expose an appendix for Acme?

If Acme prefers, we can prepare a tracked-changes doc showing only the Exhibit B fragment that will go to countersignature.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit questions — slope protection + invoice mapping

Adding legal/contract language suggestions inline below and attaching a short plain-text clause (karthik_suggested_clause.txt) for easy copy/paste. I kept both option A and B but suggested Option A (rolling 90-day) as default since it reduces month-to-month churn for both parties.

Quoted for context: "adjustments kick when monthly billable token usage changes by >15% versus rolling 90-day average (option A)..."

Suggested legal paragraph (summary):
"For purposes of Exhibit B (Slope Protection), \"Adjustment Trigger\" means a monthly billing period in which the Total Billable Tokens for Customer exceed by fifteen percent (15%) the Customer's Rolling 90-Day Average Billable Tokens. Upon an Adjustment Trigger, Redwood shall apply a smoothing factor equal to the lesser of (i) the percent difference between the Monthly Billing Period and the Rolling 90-Day Average, or (ii) ten percent (10%) of the Monthly Billing Period. Smoothing shall be applied pro rata across the affected month's invoice lines and reflected in the next invoice period as a one-time true-up, subject to the invoice mapping in Appendix 2."

Notes:
- We should be explicit about whether smoothing creates credit or a rate adjustment. I proposed a one-time true-up credit to the next invoice to keep operations simple.
- If Acme insists on %-delta approach, Karthik suggested a cap on the absolute per-month correction to avoid huge credits.

Action: Laura, please confirm the invoice appendix fields: code, description, metric reference (token units), and charge type (metered/reserved). Jordan — if the true-up credit approach is acceptable, we can convert the redline to final language and draft Appendix 2.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Pricing exhibit questions — slope protection + invoice mapping

Soojin / Karthik — thanks for the speedy turn. Acme is generally comfortable with Option A (rolling 90-day) and the true-up credit, but two clarifications before we sign:

1) Timing of the true-up: can the credit be applied on the same billing cycle as the overage is discovered (i.e., within 30 days) rather than waiting an additional full invoice period? Our finance team audits monthly and would prefer near-term credits.
2) Appendix 2: please include the following invoice fields so our AP can automate: invoice_line_code, invoice_line_description, metric_id (token), unit_multiplier, charge_type (metered/reserved). We attached our tracked-changes redline to the Exhibit B fragment (Acme_Redline_v2.docx).

We also flagged a potential edge case: when a customer has both reserved capacity and metered overage in the same month, how is smoothing allocated? We need a deterministic allocation rule. Could Redwood propose a priority (apply smoothing to metered overage first, then reserved)?

If you can incorporate those items into the final redline, we can move to countersignatures.

Best —
Jordan
Jordan Mills
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Data

Jordan — appreciate the confirmation and the tracked changes. Summary of agreed points and next actions:

Agreed items:
- We will adopt Option A (Rolling 90-Day Average) as the Adjustment Trigger with a 15% threshold and a maximum smoothing of 10% of the affected month's usage, applied as a one-time true-up credit.
- True-up timing: Redwood will apply the credit in the same billing cycle in which the Adjustment Trigger is validated (we will aim to reflect on the subsequent invoice within 30 days).
- Smoothing allocation: by default smoothing will be applied to metered overage first; any residual adjustment will flow to reserved capacity lines pro rata. This is added to Appendix 2.
- Appendix 2 invoice fields: invoice_line_code, invoice_line_description, metric_id (token), unit_multiplier, charge_type. Laura will populate Canonical Invoice Codes.

Action items and owners:
- Laura Bennett: provide canonical invoice_line_code set and draft Appendix 2 (due 2026-02-14).
- Karthik Iyer: convert the agreed paragraph into final legal language and insert allocation sentence (due 2026-02-13).
- Soojin Lee: assemble final Exhibit B bundle and send DocuSign package once legal confirms (I will upload to DocuSign and share link).
- Jordan / Acme: return countersignature within 3 business days after DocuSign is sent.

I've attached a PDF snapshot of the agreed Exhibit B for review (pricing-exhibit-final.pdf). If LAURA or KARTHIK want to make late edits, please highlight them inline; otherwise I'll route to DocuSign by EOD 2026-02-13.
